newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson proposes 6 bln skr staff debentures.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson proposes 6 bln skr staff debentures.

text.p: Swedish telecoms company Ericsson said on Thursday it was proposing an issue of convertible debentures for employees of up to a maximum of six billion crowns and an options programme for top management and key staff.
The proposal made by the board will be put to an extraordinary general meeting on September 11.
"The dramatic growth and development of the telecommunications industry continues to place high demands on Ericsson employees," Ericsson said in a statement.
Ericsson said it was investing heavily in human resource development programmes to maintain and strengthen its position in the industry and this meant a content workforce.
Under the offer, staff will be able to subscribe for debentures up to an amount of 75,000 crowns.
If employees subscribe for less than six billion crowns, this will allow future employees to be given the same opportunity to participate in the issue.
The issue is estimated to result in a dilution effect in relation to Ericsson's share capital of 1-1.5 percent.
The proposed term of the debentures will be about five and a half years. The debentures will carry interest related to STIBOR. Conversion can only take place to Ericsson's B-series shares.
The option programme for top management and key staff, effective January 1 next year, will involve about 500 people.
The distribution will be determined by the development of earnings per share and base salary and bonus categories of the relevant employees.
